panels.title: Chain tip: slot number
panels.description: cardano_node_metrics_slotNum_int -- the node's current tip slot number. Climbs steadily while syncing from genesis.

panels.title: Chain tip: block number
panels.description: cardano_node_metrics_blockNum_int -- the node's current chain height.

panels.title: Block apply rate
panels.description: deriv(cardano_node_metrics_blockNum_int[2m]) -- blocks applied per second, derived from chain-height growth. dingo_ledger_block_pipeline_blocks_validated/_decoded are intentionally not used here: they stay at 0 unless the opt-in block-processing pipeline flags are set, which this stack does not enable.

panels.title: Slots behind wall clock (tip gap)
panels.description: dingo_tip_gap_slots -- slots between the current wall-clock slot and the chain tip. Trends toward 0 as sync completes and the node reaches the chain tip.

panels.title: Chainsync header cache size
panels.description: dingo_chainsync_seen_headers -- current number of slots retained in the chainsync header deduplication cache; nonzero and moving confirms active chainsync traffic.

panels.title: Block stage latency: p50 / p99
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.50 or 0.99, sum(rate(dingo_ledger_block_stage_duration_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])) by (le, stage, variant)) -- p50 and p99 wall-clock time per ledger-owned per-block processing stage (header_verify, validate, apply). histogram_quantile is a bucket-boundary-bounded ESTIMATE, not an exact value. The buckets were widened from a ~3.3s ceiling to ~52.4s (blinklabs-io/dingo#4364: an epoch-boundary DRep voting-power query blocked block application for 4-8s, and every one of those observations previously landed in the histogram's +Inf overflow bucket, indistinguishable from any other stall past 3.3s). Watch the p99 line for this class of stall; see 'Block stage max observed duration' below for the exact worst case, which no quantile can give.

panels.title: Block stage max observed duration
panels.description: dingo_ledger_block_stage_max_duration_seconds -- the exact maximum wall-clock duration ever observed for each ledger-owned per-block stage (header_verify, validate, apply), since process start. Monotonically non-decreasing and never resets. Unlike the p50/p99 panel above, this is not a bucket-bounded estimate: it is the precise worst-ever value, which is what actually surfaces a blinklabs-io/dingo#4364-class multi-second epoch-boundary stall that the old ~3.3s histogram ceiling could not distinguish from a much larger one.
